format_version.description: Format version of the canonical procedure (descriptive metadata; not a pass/fail gate). Value is '2.0.1' for all procedures conforming to the 2.0.x format; pack/contract version is tracked separately in meta.rules_pack.

id.description: Test identifier; mirrors the H1 id in canonical text.

description.description: Description, any characters (accents, `°C`, `µ`, `±`, `≤`) but a tab, a control one (C0, DEL, C1) or a line / paragraph separator (U+2028, U+2029); may be empty or contain embedded `\n` for multi-line. Mirrors header lines after `# <id>`.

title.description: Optional human display title; one line, any characters (accents, `°C`, `µ`, `±`, `≤`) but a tab, a control one (C0, DEL, C1) or a line / paragraph separator (U+2028, U+2029). Absent or empty means the display name is the id.

_macros.description: Macro registry produced by the v2.0.2 parser. Optional; emitted only when the source contained `@LET`, `@TABLE`, or `@ALLOC` directives. Sub-keys mirror the three macro kinds; each maps a name (lowercase identifier) to its structured payload. Round-trip provenance: emitter does NOT reconstruct macro form from this field on JSON->text — the macro nodes inside `steps[]` / `expected[]` carry the authoritative form.

lets._comment: Map of @LET-bound name -> value (number, string, boolean, or expression text).

tables._comment: Map of @TABLE name -> ordered list of row objects.

allocations._comment: Map of @ALLOC name -> {start: int or its text as written, count_expr: string} block descriptor.

Meta._comment_extras: Any other key is a bench-private extra (e.g. `serial_number`, or an older procedure's `revision`): a string, kept verbatim (Canonical_Text_Procedure_v2.md, Optional keys).
Meta._comment_required: Each pack's Meta pin (`<key>: <name>@<version>`) joins these properties from its schema fragment's `meta_properties`, and is required by its fragment's allOf clause when its equipment is declared. The `board` and `requirement` keys are operator-supplied (Doc 02 §2.1, §2.2) and therefore omitted from `required` here — empty `board:` / `requirement:` slots in canonical text round-trip to absent meta keys in JSON. See per-spec rules in 02_Procedure_Json_Schema_v2.md §2.

Eq_DMM_Equipment._comment: The base-native `dmm`: an id and an optional model hint, no parameters. A pack claiming `dmm` replaces this entry with its own (its fragment's equipment_oneOf_refs).

Equipment._comment: Equipment entries carry CAPABILITY/REQUIREMENT fields (a pack's per-channel ratings, a subtype) — never BENCH-IDENTIFICATION fields (visa, port, baud, timeout, remote, manual_override), which live as module constants in the generated test.py. The base declares only its own `dmm`; each pack's equipment entries join this oneOf from its schema fragment's `equipment_oneOf_refs`.

Provenance._comment: Phase 5 Tier C unified provenance carrier (2026-04-29 evening). Replaces the prior ad hoc `expr` + `expanded_from_range` pair on step ops. `source` discriminates how the op was authored: 'range' = generated by TOKEN[A..B] + {A..B} paired-range expansion; 'explicit' = single-line author. `source_line` is the verbatim original clause text used for emit-time collapse back to the compact form. Optional; absent on ops with no expansion lineage.

RationaleString.description: Insertion rationale: any printable Unicode (excludes ASCII control chars + DEL, so no newlines). Per Doc 01 §6.2 fix 2026-04-26: relaxed from ASCII-only because real-world rationales reference rule-doc sections (e.g. 'per §6.2').

NumberOrLoopVarRef._comment: A numeric scalar field that MAY hold a `${var}` / `${row.key}` reference to a Block_for loop variable when the field appears inside a Block_for body. Outside Block_for bodies the value is always a literal number; inside, it may be a `${...}`: a name (`${name}`, `${row.key}`) or a calculation (`${i * STEP}`), its value each turn's. As of 2026-05-30 every numeric scalar field in the schema accepts this shape (the previous `NumberLiteralOnly` carve-out for timeout/probe_* fields was removed once codegen routed them through the substitution-aware `_number_expr` path). The contextual rule that string form is only permitted inside a Block_for body is enforced by the validator pass, not the schema.

Block_for._comment: Preserve-by-default `@FOR vars IN <iter> ... @ENDFOR` loop block. `vars` is an array of one or more loop-variable names (e.g., `["i"]` for range, `["i", "row"]` for table iteration). Body items can be Steps (when the loop sits inside `## Steps`) or Criteria (when inside `## Expected`).

Block_for_iter._comment: Discriminated by `kind`: `range` for integer `A..B`; `range_float` for floating-point `A..B STEP S`; `list` for `[v1, v2, ...]`; `table` for iterating rows of a `@TABLE` declared via Block_table; `name` for bare `@LET`-bound integer or table reference (disambiguated at codegen).

Range_bound_name._comment: A @FOR range bound or STEP named: a @LET or @ALLOC name, `N`, or a `${...}` (`${N}`, `${N + 1}`), read by the engine.

Block_if._comment: Preserve-by-default `@IF cond ... [@ELIF cond ...]* [@ELSE ...] @ENDIF` conditional block. The unified `branches` array holds each branch in source order; each entry has a `body` and (for non-else branches) a `condition`. Body items can be Steps or Criteria depending on whether the block sits in `## Steps` or `## Expected`.

Block_alloc._comment: Macro node: `@ALLOC name START=<expr> COUNT=<expr>` — declares a contiguous ref-block. Emitted by parser as a top-level step before any consuming `@FOR`. `count_expr`, and a `start` other than digits, are preserved as raw expression text.

Block_table._comment: Macro node: `@TABLE name ... @ENDTABLE` declaring named rows used by `@FOR i, row IN <table>` and resource lookups (`${row.<key>}`). Each row is an object whose keys are arbitrary lowercase identifiers; values are scalars (string|number|boolean) carried verbatim.

Op_abort._comment: Aborts the procedure at runtime, jumping to ## Expected evaluation and cleanup. Emitted by `@ABORT`.

Condition._comment: Phase 9.6 (Doc 04 §10): a boolean condition AST. Five leaf forms (ref-vs-value compare, ref-vs-ref compare, ref bound/unbound, loop-var-vs-value compare) plus two boolean composers (AND/OR with operands list, NOT with single operand).

Op_break._comment: `@BREAK` directive inside a Block_for/Block_do body. The validator rejects break ops outside any enclosing loop. Codegen emits Python `break` at the appropriate indent level.

Block_do._comment: Phase 9.7 (2026-05-05): `@DO <var> ... body ... @WHILE <condition> @ENDDO` run-then-check loop. Body always runs at least once. Condition is the continuation predicate (loop continues when true). The author is responsible for ensuring the predicate eventually becomes false.

Op_bind._comment: `{<ref>} = <expr> [<unit>].` bind step. `expr` is a BindExpr: an expression as an Expected line writes one, `${name}` too (a `name` node); `unit` is its value's (test.py stores the value scaled to SI). The LHS slot id may be a literal integer or, inside a loop body, an arithmetic-expression slot id (e.g. `{base+i*3+4}` -> string `'base+i*3+4'`).

ScalarOperand._comment: Phase 9.1 Doc 04 §9.6.1: a scalar operand on the right-hand side of a criterion. Either a plain `{N}` ref (RefOperand) or an aggregate over a list-typed measurement bound inside a Block_for body (AggregateOperand). Phase 9.2 adds the $defs only — existing criterion shapes still take a plain integer ref. Phase 9.5 will rewire criterion definitions to accept ScalarOperand.

Step._comment: Phase 9.2 (2026-04-30): a Step is either an op-shaped step (StepBaseFields + one of the Op_* $defs) OR a Block_for loop block. Block_for branch is preserved through parse — the parser produces Block_for nodes for `@FOR ... @END` instead of expanding them. Codegen (Phase 9.3) and validator (Phase 9.5) walk Block_for body recursively. Phase 9.6 (2026-04-30) adds three additional sibling branches: `Block_if` (`@IF ... @ENDIF` conditional), `Op_break_loop` (`@BREAK`), and `Op_bind` (`Bind {ref} = expr.`). These three branches share Block_for's structural pattern (preserve-by-default, no StepBaseFields requirement).

OpStep._comment: An op-shaped step — the pre-Phase 9.2 Step shape, factored out so Block_for can sit as a sibling branch under Step.oneOf.

Op_timestamp._comment: `Timestamp as {<ref>}.` step. Captures float seconds since procedure start, binds to a measurement ref. No equipment side effects. `ref` accepts an integer slot id or, inside a loop body, an arithmetic-expression slot id (e.g. `{base+i}` -> string).

Op_note._comment: Note step per Procedure_JSON_Schema_v2 §note: `{op: 'note', text: '<text>'}`. No `n` field — notes are preserved in source order between numbered steps but carry no step number themselves. No `source` either; notes are operator-authored prose by definition.

Op_operator_prompt._comment: Universal manual-fallback operator step per Canonical_Text_Procedure_v2 §Operator: `Operator: <free-text>.` — runtime blocks until the operator confirms. Optional `ref`: when the prose ends with `as {N}`, that {N} binds the operator's typed value (free-text equivalent of `Operator: read ... as {N}`). The `text` field carries the body verbatim (with any trailing `as {N}` stripped when ref is set).

Criterion._comment: Criterion grammar per Canonical_Text_Procedure_v2 §Expected. Discriminator field is `kind`. The parser emits structured criterion objects with kind-specific value/unit pairs (e.g., `limit_value`+`limit_unit` for lt/gt/lte/gte; `nominal_value`+`unit`+`tol_value`+`tol_unit` for tolerance_abs; `nominal_value`+`unit`+`tol_pct` for tolerance_pct). `ref` is an integer ref id at top-level expected, or a free-string arithmetic expression when inside a `block_for.body` (e.g. `'en_base + per_pin*i + 0'`).

Crit_eq._comment: Equality criterion: `<target_value> [<unit>]` (e.g., `== 0`, `== 5.0 V`); `TRUE` / `FALSE` is `true` / `false`. `target_unit` is null for unitless integer comparisons (digital reads etc.) and a unit string when comparing physical quantities.

Crit_range._comment: Range criterion `{N} in [lo_value, hi_value] [<unit>]`. A bound left out, `]lo, hi[`, is `lo_open` / `hi_open`; `not in` is `negated`; each present only when true. lo_value <= hi_value is enforced by the validator's semantic pass (EXP_RANGE_INVERTED), not by JSON Schema.

Crit_tolerance._comment: Absolute-tolerance criterion: `<nominal> [<unit>] +/- <tol> [<tol_unit>]` (e.g., `28.0 V +/- 1.0 V`, `0x10 +/- 2`); the nominal and the tolerance both carry a unit or neither does (both `null`). Parser emits as `tolerance_abs`.

Crit_percent_tolerance._comment: Percent-tolerance criterion: `<nominal> [<unit>] +/- <pct> %` (e.g., `5.0 V +/- 5 %`, `100 +/- 5 %`); `unit` is `null` when the nominal has none. Parser emits as `tolerance_pct`.

Crit_template._comment: An `## Expected` line holding a `${...}`, kept as written: in each turn each `${...}` is its value and the line it gives is read as any other (codegen, the guided run).

HexLiteral._comment: The spelling of a criterion number written in hex (`0x1A00`), kept beside its integer value so the canonical text comes back as written; present only when the text had `0x`.

LineText._comment: A text of one line: no line break of any kind (\n, \r, \u2028, ...), which would split the canonical Expected line.

CriterionRef._comment: Allowed shapes for a `ref` field (used by Criterion entries and by Op_* steps that bind/read a `{N}` ref). Three forms: (a) integer ref id (e.g. `{1}` -> 1, `{0}` -> 0); (b) string arithmetic expression (e.g. `'en_base + per_pin*i + 0'`) when the ref sits inside a `block_for.body`; (c) range object `{kind: 'range', lo, hi}` when the canonical text uses paired-range syntax `{lo..hi}` to bind a list of refs in one step.

Crit_eq_text._comment: Programmatic exact string match. Used when a step reads a discrete textual value (e.g. digital input '0'/'1') and the runtime predicate is `m == target_text`.

Crit_contains._comment: Substring test on a text reading (a bus scan, an SPI transfer, a UART answer). Runtime predicate is `target_text in m`, no strip, no case folding.

Crit_contains_any._comment: `{N} contains one of ["a", "b", ...]`: two or more texts, PASS when any is a substring of the text reading (as `contains`).

Crit_contains_all._comment: `{N} contains all of ["a", "b", ...]`: two or more texts, PASS when every one is a substring of the text reading (as `contains`).

Crit_one_of._comment: Equality with any of two or more numbers: `{N} one of [0x01, 0x02, 0x04] [<unit>]`. Each value keeps its type and, when written in hex, its spelling (`literal`); one `unit` (or `null`) for all. Same equality as `eq`.

Crit_one_of_text._comment: Equality with any of two or more texts: `{N} one of ["OK", "DONE"]`. Same equality as `eq_text`.

Crit_regex_match._comment: Regex-match criterion. Runtime predicate is `re.search(pattern, measured.strip())`. Used when a deterministic string read needs pattern matching rather than exact equality. `pattern` is preserved verbatim from the canonical text body between the `/` delimiters; `\/` escapes a literal `/`.

Crit_operator_decision._comment: Operator-judged criterion. Runtime SKIPS the predicate — the operator's verdict (PASS/FAIL/SKIP from `operator.judge`) is authoritative; the operator's free-form remark is stored as the measurement. `verdict_text` is the informational hint shown to the operator (the `(target = "...")` clause from the canonical text).

_Crit_within_pct_RENAMED_v2.0.x._comment: Tombstone: the legacy `kind: within_pct` was renamed to `kind: percent_tolerance` per `04_Expected_Expression_Grammar_v2.md` §3.8 (closed-at-ten v2.0.0 spec). Submitted JSONs using `within_pct` will fail schema validation. Codegen rewrites `kind: percent_tolerance` to legacy RULES `kind: range_abs` per Doc 04 §11, so generated test.py files keep the same eval_verdicts predicate.

_Crit_range_abs_RENAMED_v2.0.x._comment: Tombstone: the legacy `kind: range_abs` was renamed to `kind: range` per `04_Expected_Expression_Grammar_v2.md` §3.6. Codegen continues to emit legacy RULES `kind: range_abs` per Doc 04 §11.

_Crit_simple_cmp_RENAMED_v2.0.x._comment: Tombstone: the legacy `kind: lt_abs/le_abs/gt_abs/ge_abs/eq_abs` enum was split into the dedicated `kind: lt/lte/gt/gte/eq` branches per `04_Expected_Expression_Grammar_v2.md` §3.1-§3.5. Codegen continues to emit the legacy `_abs`-suffixed kinds in the generated RULES dict per Doc 04 §11.

_Crit_verdict_set_NEVER_SHIPPED_v2.0.x._comment: Tombstone: the `kind: verdict_set` form (operator picks one closed-set token, runtime predicate `m in verdicts`) was specified in early Doc 04 §3.9 drafts but never matched the actual operator workflow (operator enters a free-form remark + chooses Pass/Fail/Skip independently). Use `kind: operator_decision` instead — the criterion has no programmatic predicate; the operator's verdict is authoritative.

_Crit_is_NEVER_SHIPPED_v2.0.x._comment: Tombstone: the `kind: is` form (singleton specialization of verdict_set) was specified in early Doc 04 §3.10 drafts but never matched the operator workflow for the same reason as verdict_set. Use `kind: operator_decision` for operator-judged criteria, or `kind: eq_text` for programmatic exact-string matches.

Crit_diff._comment: Cross-measurement criterion: `{N}: {lhs_ref} - {rhs_ref} <op> <limit_value> <limit_unit>.` Single kind discriminated by the `op` field. Operand refs are NAMED (`lhs_ref` / `rhs_ref`). All ref-shaped fields accept integer ref ids OR string arithmetic expressions (the latter when the criterion sits inside a `block_for.body`).

Crit_range_abs_each._comment: `{N}: in [<lo_value>, <hi_value>] <unit> each.` — every element of the list-bound ref must lie in the closed interval. SKIP iff list is empty.

Crit_lt_each._comment: `{N}: < <value> <unit> each.` — every element strictly less than the limit.

Crit_monotonic._comment: `{N}: monotonic <mode>.` — list-bound ref must satisfy a 4-mode monotonicity predicate. Vacuously PASS for length-1 lists; SKIP for length-0.

MediaRef._comment: Per the v2 media-restoration amendment (2026-04-28): each step optionally carries a media[] array of PCB component/pin references, derived from the step text by the deterministic text parser. The procedure GUI uses these to render board images via the ODB CLI. Round-trip: text->JSON populates media; JSON->text drops it (canonical text doesn’t carry media); JSON->code does not consume it; preserving JSON->emit->parse identity requires the parser to re-derive media from text on the back-trip.

is_tp._comment: Set by the media catalogue for a test point written `TP NAME`: the component is stored without the prefix and the caption rebuilt as `TP NAME`.

Block_for_iter_range_float._comment: Float range form: `@FOR v IN A..B STEP S` where any of A/B/S is a float. Required to express continuous sweeps.

Block_for_iter_name._comment: Bare-name iterable: `@FOR i IN n` where `n` is either a `@LET`-bound integer (iterate 1..n) or a `@TABLE` reference (iterate rows). Disambiguation is deferred to codegen because both forms are syntactically identical.

Crit_aggregate._comment: Aggregate criterion: mean|min|max|sum|count|rms over a range of refs — numbers (`range_lo`, `range_hi`) or a name's as written (`ref`: `Vrail[3..7]`, `Vrail[*]`), exactly one — optionally minus a single ref, compared via op (<, <=, >, >=, =) against a numeric limit, or `in` bounds (`lo_value`, `hi_value`, the flags as Crit_range's, the unit in `limit_unit`). Parser emits this for the text forms `mean({A..B}) <op> <num> [unit].`, `mean({A..B}) - {N} <op> <num> [unit].` and `mean({A..B}) [not] in [lo, hi] [unit].`.

Crit_eq_digital._comment: Digital-logic equality: `{N}: == '0'.` or `{N}: == '1'.`. Disambiguates from PWM-duty equality (`{N}: == 1.` parses as eq with target_value=1). Use this form when the ref holds a digital read (a pack op binding a `digital` reading). The single quotes mirror the Set-side digital-write dispatch syntax.

Crit_expr._comment: `<expr> <cmp> <expr>` — general expression comparison. Used when neither side reduces to a single ref or a recognized prefix form (e.g. `{1} <= {2} + 0.8 V`, `{1} <= {2} + {3}`, `{1} = {2}`). A unit follows a number (`lit.unit`); the criterion has none of its own.

Crit_expr_in._comment: `<expr> in [lo, hi] [<unit>]` — a range on a computed value (`{3} / 256 in [20, 30]`): the bounds, unit and flags of Crit_range, `lhs` names at least one ref and its numbers carry no unit. A lone ref is Crit_range.

Crit_logic._comment: `or` / `and` over two or more full criteria (`{1} < 1 or {1} > 2`, `({1} < 1 or {1} > 2) and {2} = "OK"`). A part with the same `op` is flattened in; one with the other `op` is a parenthesised group. Verdict (Kleene): `or` PASS when a part passes, FAIL when every part fails; `and` FAIL when a part fails, PASS when every part passes; SKIP otherwise. A part of the same `op` as its parent is refused: it is written flattened.

ExprNode._comment: Recursive expression AST for Crit_expr. Leaves are ref / lit / str / char, internal nodes are binop with `+ - * /` or a bit operation `& | << >>` (IntOperand; a shift by a literal is 0 to 512), and abs (`abs(<expr>)`). An operand of arithmetic, of abs and a side of Crit_expr is an Operand. Rules the schema cannot express, the parser keeps: a side of numbers alone in a bit operation exactly whole (EXP_BITS_ON_DECIMAL), a unit on a criterion holding a bit operation anywhere or on a factor of `*` / `/`, a number added to a reading without the unit its line carries elsewhere, bounds holding no number (EXP_RANGE_INVERTED), and readings a step binds as decimals in a bit operation (EXP_BITS_ON_DECIMAL).

Operand._comment: An operand of arithmetic, of abs() and a side of Crit_expr: a number, a single ref or arithmetic — never text (str / char) nor a ref range, which no evaluator can compute.

IntOperand._comment: A side of a bit operation (`& | << >>`): no number with a unit anywhere below, no literal that is no integer. One of numbers alone exactly whole (else EXP_BITS_ON_DECIMAL), the parser keeps; any other a run computes (not computed when it is no whole number).

NoUnitOperand._comment: An operand inside a bit operation: no number with a unit, at any depth.

BindExpr._comment: A Bind's right-hand side: an expression as an Expected line writes one — refs, numbers with no unit (the Bind's `unit` is its value's), `+ - * /`, bit operations, abs — plus the macro values `${name}` / `${row.key}` (name) and `COUNT(<table>)` (count), and an aggregate of a ref range (`mean({1..3})`). The parser keeps what the schema cannot: a whole side of numbers alone in a bit operation, no constant divisor 0, no text.

Unit._comment: A unit of the one unit table (rules_packager_base.test_helpers.UNITS), or `%` — never empty.

Op_call._comment: `Call <module>.<function>(<arg>, ...)[ (timeout = <t> <unit>)][ as <out>, ...].` step: runs a project function (functions/<module>.py) on values and binds what it returns. `args` is always present; `timeout` / `timeout_unit` and `outputs` only when written. An output's `ref` is an integer slot id or the text written (a name, arithmetic, a range `11..20`, `H[1..10]`); its `unit` is the unit the function returns (stored in SI). The parser keeps what the schema cannot: no name part starting with `_` or a Python keyword, keywords after positionals and once each, a time limit above 0.

CallArg._comment: A Call argument: its value, the unit it was written with (passed in SI), its keyword `name` when written `name=value`.

CallValue._comment: A Call argument's value: a ref (a name range or `[*]` as written: a list), a range of refs (a list), a number (`true` / `false` for TRUE / FALSE; a hex one keeps its spelling), a minus sign on a number (a hex one), a quoted text, a `${name}`.
